Situations / Warren Situation

The Warren — Active Hub

Situation

The Warren is the only fixed Rattkin settlement in the Shattered Sea: 200–250 permanent residents, the largest single Run in the Passage, and the anchor point for the network’s memory. Perrin can reach it, but doing so brings the party into a guarded intelligence culture with three active pressure points already in motion.

Current State

The Tangle has reasons to engage Perrin if he returns: Nona and Anzolo are already searching for him, the secret Below project makes Perrin’s silence a liability, they can route the Surety disguise work, and they have three Calveno problems suited to capable outsiders. The party should experience the Warren as useful, wary, and transactional without becoming cold. Its trust starts dry-but-watched.

Toy Fields

FieldValue
VerbRemembers. The Warren converts routes, favours, debts, and threats into long-term leverage.
Unstable ConditionPerrin is silent after the Vestra loss, Passage surface operations are leaking, and two courier incidents point at compromised Calveno routes.
ConsequenceHelping the Warren creates deep Tangle credit; mishandling it chills Perrin’s strongest network.
Link of RelevancePerrin is family; Jean-Claude’s anti-slavery history creates rare common ground; Calveno ship-disguise access runs through this hub.

Key Facts

  • The Tangle is seven senior elders holding the Passage’s most sensitive routing intelligence.
  • Perrin Black-Jaw’s family is the Tangle; he knows routes, protocols, and people travelling-Run Rattkin do not.
  • The Tangle has received four non-Rattkin guests in the last century.
  • Dravosi Crown does not know the Warren exists as a fixed settlement.
  • The Seven Houses know Rattkin exist in Calveno but not the Warren’s location or scale.
  • Andriana Trevisan knows roughly where it is but will not name a contact or lead anyone there.

The Below

The Below is the Tangle’s evacuation strategy: a Tier 4 habitat carrack under construction at Kalowe. Kin name: the Below. Dry commission name: Saltmarsh Trader. The Chain Council authorized the commission without knowing the true purpose; three representatives signed, none understanding what they bought.

Purpose: carry 400 Rattkin, the Tangle Chamber, and the Memory Hold archive to open water if Calveno ever exposes the Warren. Perrin’s silence since the Vestra sank makes the elders ask whether he can still be trusted to carry knowledge of it.

Triggers:

  • Perrin makes contact and establishes whether he is still Kin in their eyes
  • Crown genealogical records or Calveno politics move closer to the Run
  • Chain Council discovers the true purpose of the commission
  • The party reaches Kalowe and sees the project without context

Active Leads

Bela Silt-Paw — Sub-Level Survey

Full details: Warren — Bela Silt-Paw. Bela is trapped in flooded drainage tunnels with a broken forearm, a message shard, and 2–3 days left. A Water Weird holds the central chamber. Reward: 200 gp + Tangle goodwill + harbour-foundation route. Cache: 340 gp + 2 potions of water breathing + Commendant Ulrik Faste’s fraudulent supply contract dispatch (~500 gp value).

Marrow’s Crate — Dead Courier

Full details: Warren — Marrow’s Crate. A crate delivered by Dry runner Dren (now dead) has gone unclaimed for three weeks. Crate contents: Vretek/Brol letter, 280 gp in Tessarine silver, House Vretek signet ring (120 gp). Serin Haut killed Dren and is watching the canal approaches. Her room: codebook (500 gp), 420 gp, informant list, and Ferrin Locke’s cooperation agreement.

Ferrin Locke — The Leak

Full details: Warren — Ferrin Locke. Three Passage surface operations were intercepted. The common channel leads to Ferrin Locke, a Dry canal broker coerced by Petra Venn, a Dravosi intelligence attaché posing as a Tessarine trade arbitration consultant. Ferrin wants out. Venn’s next check-in is 9 days after inquiry begins.

Nona — Table Frame

Use the public Nona page for what the world can know. Keep this here for table-facing work: she has been at war her whole life and stayed anyway. The food is what all of this is for, not a way to work the room. She sees guests clearly from the first moment and will tell them what she sees, but only after they have eaten.

Voice cues:

“Eat. You look like a starved little mouse. Ruk dear, more stew for the cleric.” “Never snatch. Snatching is for children and amateurs. Smile. Sit. Eat. Make them decide to be generous.” “Enzo, if they reach for steel before bread, break only one hand. We are not animals.”

Nona’s pressure points. She does not yet know the Vestra is gone. When she learns, she will feel the family grief and the Passage logistics at the same time — the ship was both.

What she is really afraid of is not that something happened to Perrin. It is that something happened to him — that the silence means he’s drifting from what she built him to be.

Her instructions to Anzolo, if it comes up at the table:

“Find my boy. If he is hiding, bring him home. If he is hurt, bring me the one who hurt him. If he is dead, bring me the truth, and do not soften it. I am old, not fragile.”

Nona’s Inner Circle

Enzo — black jaguar tabaxi, obsidian-furred with rosettes visible in the light and a pale scar along the left side of his jaw. Tailored suit, immaculate shoes. Rarely speaks. Communicates through a lit cigar, a held door, and the slow unsheathing of one claw. His sentence is “Nona asked you a question.”

Ruk — massive scarred lizardfolk. Heavy muscle and occasional sous-chef. Literal, observant, terrible at pretending not to notice things. Useful as a barometer — if Ruk has gone quiet and is watching someone specifically, that is not a good sign for them.

The Rattle

The Warren’s community warning system — built by Nona Black-Jaw decades ago to alert the settlement to Dravosi attempts at subjugation. A Rattkin strikes a pan in a specific rhythm. The sound carries through kitchens, vents, and stone — each household passes it on, pan to pan, until the noise fills the district in under thirty seconds. To any outsider it is cooking noise, unremarkable and legally unactionable. To Kin it is the sound of their home going to war.

The cascade: One pan starts it. Within five seconds every kitchen within earshot picks up the rhythm. Within fifteen seconds the sound has travelled through stone and pipe and vent duct into every corner of the Warren. Within thirty seconds every Rattkin in the district knows.

The response: Not military formation — guerrilla resistance from every member of the community, however they can. Mothers block sight lines with laundry. Children carry messages through rat-runs too small for Dravosi. Elders bar doors that look decorative until they’re barred. Fighters move to positions Nona mapped twenty years ago. Shop owners produce weapons from false bottoms in flour barrels. Everyone moves. No one waits.

Two quick taps after silence: the threat is clear. Life resumes as if nothing happened.

Nona built this because the Crown’s raids on Le Paludi settlements were silent, fast, and relied on surprise. The Rattle removes surprise. It converts a Dravosi raid into a fight against a community that was ready before the first boot hit the cobblestones.

DM Note

If the party hears the Rattle while inside the Warren, treat it as a timed pressure: Kin are moving to positions, routes are closing, and the window for civilian behaviour is narrowing fast. The party is not a threat, but they are inside a community that has just shifted from peacetime to wartime in under a minute. The Rattle is not an abstraction. It is the sound of two hundred people deciding simultaneously to fight.

Access Mechanics

Plausible paths to entry: service to a Run in danger, a threat neutralized against the Calveno Hold, or Fancy Rat relationship built over multiple sessions. Il Velo makes Rattkin movement easier because a Fancy Rat in a crowd reads as costume.

Tone. The Warren is not a thieves’ guild quest board. It is a kin-state with memory. Offers are phrased as reviews, routing help, cache rights, or future access. Coin appears, but the real currency is whether the Tangle changes what doors open for Perrin.

Perrin Family Clock

Nona has activated a circuit-wide Passage inquiry because Perrin’s silence has gone on too long. Anzolo has worked the Passage contacts between Calveno and the Central Strait and found nothing.

Outcomes:

  • Perrin contacts Nona first: the Vestra conversation happens on his terms
  • Anzolo finds him first: it happens on Nona’s terms, with a witness
  • No contact next interval: Nona escalates; Anzolo is not her last card

Locations

  • Tangle Chambers — archive and summons-only seat
  • The Low Lamp — communal tavern; unclaimed message shard hook
  • Marrow’s — deniable cargo broker; dead courier crate
  • The Splint — apothecary; suspicious injury clue

Consequences

  • Warren helped cleanly: Perrin gains real Tangle credit, usable later when the party needs routes, papers, or protection.
  • Warren treated carelessly: access remains possible but cold, expensive, and watched.
  • Intelligence sold outward: short-term coin, long-term Passage suspicion.
  • Jean-Claude trusted: Rattkin anti-slavery policy gives him a rare non-Grung ally base.
  • Perrin delays too long: the Tangle treats the Vestra loss as a liability and reassesses his standing around the Below.
